question:
A 26-year-old female patient comes to the office reporting hip pain for the past two weeks. She
describes the pain as dull and constant, which intensifies during extended periods of sitting. Ibuprofen
has provided minimal relief. While she denies any recent trauma, she mentions starting a new exercise
routine involving cycling and jogging. The structural examination reveals the following measurements: *
Distance from umbilicus to left ASIS: 3 cm * Distance from umbilicus to right ASIS: 5 cm * Distance
from umbilicus to left ischial tuberosity: 5 cm * Distance from umbilicus to right ischial tuberosity: 3 cm *
Standing flexion test: Positive on the left side What is the most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A)
right innominate outflare (B) left innominate outflare (C) left innominate inflare (D) left posterior
innominate rotation (E) piriformis syndrome (F) iliopsoas tendinitis (G) left hip impingement syndrome
(H) left innominate posterior rotation (I) trochanteric bursitis (J) sacroiliac joint dysfunction
 A. right innominate outflare
B. trochanteric bursitis
C. left innominate outflare
D. left innominate inflare
E. iliopsoas tendinitis
F. left posterior innominate rotation
G. left hip impingement syndrome
H. piriformis syndrome
I. left innominate posterior rotation
J. sacroiliac joint dysfunction
